{"disposition":"return_to_vendor","reasoning":"INV-1013 is returned to the vendor under F1, F2, F3, and F4. F1 is a total mismatch: line items sum to $21,040.00 and tax is $1,472.80, so lines plus tax equal $22,512.80, but the stated total is $22,562.80. F2, F3, and F4 are quantities over what we can accept (WidgetA 22 vs 15 in stock, WidgetB 18 vs 10, GadgetX 9 vs 5), which the vendor can correct and resubmit.","vendor_reply":"Hello Atlas Industrial Supply billing team,

We cannot process invoice INV-1013 as submitted. The line items sum to $21,040.00 and tax is $1,472.80, so lines plus tax equal $22,512.80, but the invoice total is $22,562.80 ($50.00 higher). WidgetA is billed at a combined quantity of 22, WidgetB at 18, and GadgetX at 9, which are more than we can accept.

Please send a corrected invoice that reduces those quantities, recalculates each line amount, tax, and any shipping, and shows a total that equals lines plus tax plus shipping.

Thank you,
Acme Corp Accounts Payable"}

The corrected invoice must reconcile its total to the line items plus tax. The line items sum to $21,040 and tax is $1,472.80.

The audit log reasoning can cite internal stock levels because it is for internal use only. The exact quantities are 22 for WidgetA, 18 for WidgetB, and 9 for GadgetX.

The vendor email body is drafted. It cites the $50.00 total mismatch and requests a corrected invoice whose total equals line items plus tax plus shipping.
